decision: break_credit_multiplier defaults to 3.0 in the standard ergonomic profile and 2.0 in default, relaxed, strict and demo; the struct fallback stays 2.0
rationale: 3.0 gives a 45 min sit : 15 min break ratio, which matches how the owner actually works; the other profiles keep their existing pace

decision: current_session_secs is deleted from SessionState, SessionStateDto and StateChangedPayload; the Debug tab alone gets secs_since_last_break, and no timer, bar, colour or notification may read it
rationale: the popup timer read the uncredited counter and dropped to zero on every return to sitting, contradicting the break credit the engine had applied; deleting the field makes the compiler enforce one credited counter instead of a convention

decision: E015 ships before the public release (E017)
rationale: the visible symptom is a timer that resets on standing; shipping a release with it teaches users the wrong model

decision: MoveUp is released under the MIT licence; LICENSE at the repo root carries the standard MIT text with copyright holder "Paweł Żentała", and the same licence is declared in package.json and src-tauri/Cargo.toml
rationale: the open-core model keeps the desktop app itself open and sells the cloud/AI layer, so the app needs a permissive licence that lets anyone build, fork and ship it; MIT is the shortest such licence and the one the surrounding ecosystem already assumes

decision: ts-rs generates the TypeScript mirror of every Rust DTO into src/generated/; src/types.ts and SettingsTypes.ts re-export it, and E015's fixture-based drift test is deleted
rationale: hand-typed mirrors drifted silently - the codegen immediately exposed three live drifts (TodaySummary missing three fields, SessionEntry typing a nullable duration as number and omitting break_credit, DeskSettings still declaring five fields that moved to the profiles); a compile error is stronger than a runtime key-set diff. specta was rejected as a larger commitment: its value is generating invoke() command bindings, which means rewiring every call site
scope: src-tauri DTO structs, src/generated/, src/types.ts, src/components/settings/SettingsTypes.ts

decision: the session engine derives a day boundary from the injected instant's LOCAL calendar day, not its UTC day; needs_daily_reset_at and check_daily_reset_at take that local date as an explicit argument
rationale: every other date-keyed surface in this repo (session_persistence.rs, db_sessions.rs) already keys off the local day, so comparing UTC days made the in-memory daily reset fire hours away from the persisted "today" for any user east or west of UTC; no alternative was considered, because the UTC-day comparison was the outlier rather than a choice anyone made

decision: the phone is the bridge and the watch is a glance surface: voice capture and health relay both run on the phone, and the watch receives replies only by mirroring the phone's notifications
rationale: running our own code on the Galaxy Watch 4 means a Wear OS app, a second build chain and a pairing story for one user; Android's notification mirroring delivers the output half for free, and the input half is not worth the platform

decision: health data enters through a source-agnostic HealthSource trait plus a HealthAggregator and an authenticated LAN push inlet (POST /display/health); Google Fit becomes one registered source rather than the architecture
rationale: ADR 012 claimed a backend swap would be local to ~3 files, but the vendor's name was in the command names, DTO names and component name, so Fit's announced end-of-life was a rewrite; the phone's Health Connect data is on-device only and can therefore only be pushed, which needs an endpoint the app owns
scope: src-tauri/src/health_source.rs, health_models.rs, remote_routes_health.rs, remote_auth.rs, google_fit_service.rs, commands_health.rs, src/hooks/useHealth.ts, src/components/HealthWidget.tsx

decision: a parsed voice intent is an event, never an engine input: it is written to events.log and the voice_notes table and acknowledged, and the only side effect any intent has is Snooze setting CommunicationPolicy's existing snooze fields; nothing on the voice path calls into session_*.rs or mutates SessionState
rationale: ADR 015 makes the session engine a pure core and a voice route is an adapter; letting a spoken 'I am walking' set DeskState would give the engine two contradictory sources of truth about position, with reconciliation rules (sensor disagrees, what ends a spoken walk) that are a feature with its own design rather than a side effect of this handler

decision: the tier line runs between local and hosted: the LAN inlets, the intent parser, the capture UI and the outbound webhook ship in the open app, while the AI reply is bring-your-own-key (the user's own OPENROUTER_API_KEY) and hosted AI coaching plus cloud relay stay Pro
rationale: ADR 005's open-core model sells the cloud layer, not the desktop app; a BYOK reply costs us nothing to ship, cannot be the paid product, and an absent key is the feature being off rather than an error

decision: keyboard dictation into a textarea is the primary voice path and the browser's SpeechRecognition is progressive enhancement, shown only when window.SpeechRecognition exists and navigator.permissions does not report the microphone as denied
rationale: Chrome reserves SpeechRecognition for secure contexts and /display is served over plain http://<LAN-IP>:3390 (ADR 001), so making it primary would make the primary path the one that fails on the deployment we actually have; OS keyboard dictation works on any origin, so inverting the order puts the reliable path first and hides the fragile one when it is unavailable

decision: Google Fit is not removed; it stays a registered source and the health widget's tooltip carries a dated 'Google Fit ends late 2026' hint while it is the only source producing the snapshot
rationale: the API still works and still holds the user's history, so removing it early costs data for no gain; with the HealthSource trait in place its eventual shutdown is a source that stops registering, which makes the dated warning the whole migration plan the user needs to see

decision: the cross-device relay runs on Cloudflare Workers with one Durable Object per desk and D1 for credential rows, not on pve01.lan and not on a managed pub/sub vendor; the room holds the latest snapshot in memory and no history
rationale: a paid, customer-facing service cannot depend on a home box behind NAT with autosleep and no SLA, and knowdlege/my-severs.md reserves self-hosting for our own services; WebSocket hibernation makes an idle desk cost nothing, D1 is SQLite which the app already speaks, and wrangler dev runs the whole relay locally for tests; a managed pub/sub would replace our pairing model with the vendor's, and auth is the decision this epic is about

decision: authentication is a pairing code that mints long-lived per-device tokens (mu_d_/mu_v_ prefix, 32 random bytes, SHA-256 at rest, constant-time compare, never in a URL) with no accounts, no e-mail and no passwords; the desk token lives in the OS credential store via keyring and revocation is a per-device list in desktop Settings
rationale: one shared secret cannot be revoked per phone, carries no identity to route a command_result back or to name in an audit line, and accounts would make this epic's first act storing an e-mail address in a privacy-first product; a license key plus device tokens is the smallest revocable surface, and an account can later be layered on as the thing that owns license keys without discarding these tables

decision: two-way control v1 is exactly three allowlisted commands — ack_alert, set_limits {sit_min 5..=240, stand_min 1..=120, at least one} and switch_profile {kind, name} — validated on the relay and again on the desk, refused when older than 30 s, executed through the same functions the desktop UI calls and logged to events.log; calibration and a generic save_settings are out
rationale: each of the three maps 1:1 to an existing validated function with its clamps already in place, so the remote path adds no new way to reach an invalid state; calibration from a phone is meaningless because the person is not at the desk, and a generic settings write from an untrusted network is exactly what a security reviewer rejects

decision: the LAN path stays as the free tier: remote_server.rs is modified in place rather than forked, wraps its events in the same v1 envelope, remains read-only (an inbound frame is logged at debug and dropped) and gains AppConfig.remote_lan_enabled defaulting to true; closing the zero-auth-on-LAN gap with LAN pairing is filed in the backlog rather than done here
rationale: one envelope means one React client for both transports instead of a forked useRemoteDesk, and keeping the LAN path read-only means the app's first remote write path is the authenticated one — the unauthenticated surface never gains a write; the tier table already promises 'your own Wi-Fi, view only' for free and 'anywhere, control, revocable devices' for Pro, so narrowing the LAN gap with a toggle matches what was sold

decision: the relay hostname is relay.desk.zentala.io, a subdomain of the product domain, held as the constant RELAY_DEFAULT_URL and overridable in Settings (an empty value clamps back to the default); deploying to it goes through consent-broker
rationale: a constant with an override lets staging and a self-hosted relay work without a rebuild, which is what keeps ADR 022's vendor risk contained — the protocol, not the host, is the contract; deploying to a customer-facing hostname is outward-facing and therefore a gated action rather than a step in a task

decision: T16 (deploy the relay to relay.desk.zentala.io) is deferred indefinitely; the epic stays code-complete but not deployed, and the app ships with the LAN-only free tier as the live remote-display path
rationale: the relay's two Durable Object classes (DeskRoom, RateLimiter) cannot run on Cloudflare's free plan -- Workers Paid (5 USD/month, flat, ongoing) is a hard requirement, not a usage overage; presented the cost and three alternatives (pay and deploy, self-host on the homelab instead of Cloudflare, or stay LAN-only) and Pawel chose to stay LAN-only rather than commit to the recurring cost right now
scope: relay/wrangler.toml (database_id stays a placeholder), .plan/epics/E022-2026-09-06-cross-device-phone-relay/HANDOFF.md (T16), DNS for relay.desk.zentala.io (never created)
